newsitem.title: USA: Coke to begin testing embossed beverage can.
newsitem.headline: Coke to begin testing embossed beverage can.

text.p: The Coca Cola Company said on Thursday that it is on track to begin test marketing a new embossed aluminum can for Sprite in North Western U.S. by early June.
Company's spokeswoman, Polly Howes said limited testing would take place in Portland, Ore. perhaps within the next ten days.

The embossed can includes indentation where current Sprite cans have bubbles and a tear-like design known among Coke executives as "silver streak". Coke also says the can is designed with high registration graphics that appear clearer to the eye of the consumer.

George Gourlay, senior vice-president and manager of Coke's technical operations division, told the Aluminum Association's Alumitech 97 conference that the embossed can is another indication of the company's new strategy of using packaging to increase perceived value for consumers.
He said the innovative features "give this can a really incredible appearance, a wonderful feel".
Gourlay said the arrival of the embossed can follows a positive response to contour shaped cans introduced for Coke Classic last March in Indiana, Texas, Arizona and New Mexico.

He said it was still too early to know the results of the contour can test marketing initiative but told conference delegates that consumers say they like the look, the feel and, in some cases, say it makes the product taste better.
